# RustRed status — 17 September 2026

## 1. Executive status and scope of this checkpoint

This is a stable-development checkpoint requested before a quota pause, not a
declaration that the four-loop goal is finished. New feature work has stopped.
The checkpoint consolidates the existing implementation, tests, independent
reviews and measurements, with unfinished tasks explicitly identified.

The production baseline is the shipped one-, two- and three-loop single-scale
vacuum functionality. RustRed generates K1/K3/K6 artifacts, and Vakint ships the
corresponding data and offline master projections. The previously recorded
through-three-loop selection passed **83 tests** on the published Symbolica 3
stack. That is a historical regression result, not a fresh run of those 83
tests during this checkpoint and not a count of 83 distinct integrals.

Four-loop candidate generation now works for all four external parent families
H, X, BMW and FG. The experimental Vakint bridge has also passed **12 concrete
numerical comparisons**, three per parent, against FMFT. This is substantial
progress, but it is **not** the full four-loop native acceptance suite. There
is still no independently certified, cold-reloadable four-loop artifact shipped
with Vakint, and no complete shipped four-loop terminal catalog.

Here K is the number of scalar-product coordinates in a complete vacuum family:
K = L(L+1)/2, hence K6 at three loops and K10 at four loops. A physical parent
may use fewer propagators; the remaining coordinates represent irreducible
numerators. Family definitions, physical slots and requested sectors are input
data. None of the new solver work identifies a graph by its topology name.

The goal's three parallel lanes remain:

| Lane | Owner during checkpoint | Scientific status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Symbolica reconstruction | `reconstruction_matrix`; independent implementation and measurement reviews | All four parents complete with one and six workers; all saved outputs match sparse exact |
| Original C++ SpIRed and output comparison | `cpp_output_equivalence`; independent measurement review | H/FG/X complete in both configurations, BMW serial complete; BMW six-worker remains censored |
| Vakint four-loop application and certification | `/root` integration, `semi_pivot_audit` validation/timing | Twelve finite-target comparisons pass; full acceptance, four-loop certification and production delivery remain open |

The detailed terminal evidence and final publication outcome are recorded below
and in the linked benchmark report. A stopped or interrupted job is never
counted as a completed solver workload.

## 2. Four-loop IBP generation: what has been measured

The comparison uses the same external H/X/BMW/FG routing inputs, natural
coordinate ordering, sixteen ordinary IBP sources, numerical-case search depth
two and complete requested nonzero-sector manifests. All physical-parent
subsectors are requested; auxiliary coordinates stay nonpositive. The four
campaigns overlap, so their counts must not be added and called a globally
deduplicated master basis.

These are **solver-only seconds**, excluding preparation, file output,
independent certification and compilation. Each cell lists **one worker / six
workers**. The C++ runs use the optimized original solver; only the approved
driver ordering-resolution correction is retained. Rust uses release builds.

| Parent | C++ SpIRed | RustRed sparse exact | RustRed Symbolica reconstruction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H | 3182.388 / 1987.631 | 105.649 / 33.305 | 541.876 / 65.878 |
| FG | 2234.175 / 278.706 | 62.305 / 29.251 | 191.468 / 71.996 |
| BMW | 24390.850 / checkpoint-censored | 116.480 / 64.690 | 383.279 / 395.940 |
| X | 44791.610 / 27500.180 | 299.662 / 103.340 | 894.666 / 593.857 |

These are individual observations on a shared machine, not controlled repeated
performance guarantees. Runs used fixed affinity, but unrelated machine load
was not excluded. Some later reconstruction observations used different
physical cores from the older sparse baseline. In particular, the large H
serial/parallel ratio and the poor BMW reconstruction scaling should not be
presented as predictable multicore speedups. BMW reconstruction actually used
more CPU time with six workers and did not improve wall time.

The recorded 900-second C++ terminations remain historical timeouts; incomplete
terminal records for other initial observations are labelled separately.
The subsequent uncapped BMW serial run really completed after about **6.78
hours** of solving; it is not a timeout substituted into a ratio. The supplied
small `vac4.cpp` example selects only 27 sectors and is a different workload.
Its much shorter historical timing is not comparable with these full parents.
The uncapped BMW six-worker run was stopped for this checkpoint after
3,005.99 seconds wall time, 5,251.41 seconds CPU and 2,189,212 KiB peak RSS.
It produced no final rules and has no completed solver timing. Subsequent
uncapped X six-worker and serial runs completed successfully; their full
chronology and output checks are recorded in the generation comparison. All
checkpoint-owned benchmark jobs have now stopped.

The generation outputs also differ in size and terminal basis:

| Parent | Requested nonzero sectors | RustRed rules / finite residuals | Completed C++ rules / finite residuals |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H | 314 | 21,360 / 386 | 21,297 / 442 |
| FG | 124 | 9,272 / 145 | 9,224 / 188 |
| BMW | 134 | 9,024 / 179 | 8,957 / 250 |
| X | 328 | 19,980 / 445 | 19,803 / 597 |

RustRed sparse-exact files are byte-identical between one and six workers for
every parent. All eight reconstruction outputs match sparse exact byte for
byte: all 1,808 files were checked, including every requested sector and
rule/residual count, with an independent repeat of the validation.
Completed C++ H and FG outputs match their own serial/six-worker counterparts
byte for byte. These are strong reproducibility checks but are not mathematical
identity or closure certificates.

C++ and RustRed cannot be compared by byte equality: their representations and
finite master sets differ. RustRed deliberately preserves the full homogeneous
identity in the shared numerical-case solver, rather than reproducing the
identified reference defect, and retains explicit activation guards. The
comparison lane therefore additionally reduces concrete C++ outputs into the
RustRed terminal basis and checks exact coefficient differences with Symbolica.
All twelve concrete cross-solver canaries passed: four H, three FG and five
BMW targets. The main recurrence comparisons contain 248 versus 285 terms
for H, 78 versus 99 for FG, and 179 versus 217 for BMW before basis transport;
after transport every symbolic coefficient agrees exactly. These finite checks
are distinct from checking every parametric formula over its whole domain;
raw count agreement alone is never called equivalence.

Full wall/CPU/RSS measurements, binary identities, interrupted-run chronology,
file counts and worker restrictions are in
[the generation comparison](docs/four_loop_generation_comparison.md). Generated
benchmark outputs and frozen executables are retained as local, unpublished
evidence; their paths are recorded in that report. No reference sources are
published to the RustRed repository.

## 3. What changed in reconstruction, and what has not

The failing semi-numerical route was not repaired by implementing a separate
rational-reconstruction library. It continues to use Symbolica's development
API for finite-field algebra, sparse elimination and rational-polynomial
reconstruction. Sparse-exact generation remains available independently, and
the existing candidate/artifact schemas are retained.

Several distinct failure mechanisms needed attention. A generic rational
target row must not be reconstructed by mixing samples from different pivot
branches. Merely recording the final set of pivot columns is insufficient:
different source rows can become dependent at exceptional sample points and
produce the same pivot-column sequence with a different meaning. The audited
implementation records the source-by-source outcomes, including dependent
rows, so the branch identity retains that chronology.

Support discovery must also vary coordinates independently. The earlier
affine-line sampling could miss a nonzero coefficient such as a factor that
vanishes along that entire line. The current regression tests explicitly
exercise this problem and the corrected sampling. Sampled support is discovery
evidence, never a proof that other coefficients vanish.

Finally, reconstruction is compared with the exact sparse target row. A
reconstruction miss may trigger an exact support check; a disagreement can
trigger a bounded reconstruction retry with the exact support. Nonzero
unresolved coefficients still fail closed. There is no silent declaration of
closure from successful sampling.

This checkpoint therefore measures **reconstruction plus its internal exact
sparse check**, not a reconstruction-only workload and not independent
artifact certification. It is currently slower than sparse exact in the
completed matched cells. The full-parent matrix uses a retained frozen binary;
the later source-chronology and sampling regression corrections are identified
separately in its provenance notes. Timing from that binary must not be
relabelled as a new benchmark of every later source revision.

No new Symbolica patch is introduced by this reconstruction repair. Further
optimization of repeated finite-field preparation, reconstruction probes or
ordering choices is deferred. The checkpoint is meant to preserve a working,
auditable base, not to add another unmeasured optimization immediately before
the pause.

## 4. Vakint numerical coverage and FMFT comparison

The four-loop bridge is explicitly experimental and opt-in. RustRed owns
candidate-rule application and the exact terminal decomposition. Vakint uses
its existing topology matching/routing information, the FeynKit tensor path
and its existing pure-Rust master-finalization machinery. The ordinary
production four-loop RustRed backend is not silently enabled without artifacts.
Existing defaults and FORM-backed evaluation modes remain available.

For each parent, the experiment compares the corner, a dotted parent and a
pinch. BMW uses a first-slot power of three: its original power-two target was
already a declared terminal, and the test correctly demanded a genuinely
recurrence-applying target. The resulting native cold comparisons perform:

| Parent | New rule applications for dotted target | Numerical comparisons |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| H | 26,956 | 3 passed |
| FG | 3,362 | 3 passed |
| X | 82,637 | 3 passed |
| BMW, first power 3 | 16,113 | 3 passed |

The native comparison uses an invalid FORM executable path after explicitly
separate offline terminal preparation. It does not fall back to FORM during
scalar application. However, running this development experiment from scratch
still uses FMFT/FORM to prepare exact projections for the terminals actually
reached. A fully shipped four-loop catalog that removes that setup dependency
is unfinished. No claim of new 20,000-digit master data is made.

The **15 existing legacy FMFT reference entrypoints also pass**: fourteen
analytic four-loop tests and the decorated freeform test whose name mentions
one loop but whose input is four-loop. These are a separate regression gate,
not fifteen native RustRed acceptance passes. The twelve experimental probes
do not cover the full existing numerator, mass and topology inventory.

A real shared-finalizer bug was corrected: exact Laurent coefficients are
expanded before substituting approximate master-table constants. Otherwise
exact cancellations could appear as tiny floating poles and fail an unchanged
relative comparison. The regression reproduces that distinction; no tolerance,
master precision, unknown-order rejection or default normalization was relaxed.
The existing precision-warning path warns when requested working precision
exceeds supplied master precision. Increasing working precision does not create
additional digits of source master data.

The matched timing results make the cold/warm distinction essential. These
are medians of three repeats, in seconds, with numerical parity checked:

| Dotted target and evaluation boundary | FMFT | RustRed cold | RustRed warm |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H, scalar | 3.168 | 38.271 | 0.0336 |
| H, FeynKit plus evaluation | 1.934 | 37.749 | 0.0349 |
| FG, scalar | 0.968 | 1.873 | 0.0406 |
| FG, FeynKit plus evaluation | 0.969 | 1.868 | 0.294 |
| BMW power three, scalar | 2.628 | 16.481 | 0.0586 |
| BMW power three, FeynKit plus evaluation | 0.701 | 4.477 | 0.0612 |

Generation and offline master preparation are excluded from these intervals.
FMFT subprocess startup and I/O are included. All timed results are numerically
compared afterward; parent RSS snapshots are not per-phase peak measurements
and do not capture a FORM child's peak memory. The frozen correctness build is
release-optimized with LTO disabled, not the repository's unmodified full-LTO
benchmark profile. Shared-host variation also explains why medians from the
separate full/scalar observations are not perfectly nested.

"Cold" here means the candidate's reduction memo cache is cleared, not that
all Symbolica/OS state is reset or a fresh process is launched for each repeat.
Observed resident snapshots were about 935,000 KiB for H, 307,000 KiB for FG and
592,000–596,000 KiB for BMW. These include the live prepared process, not just one cache
entry, and must not be relabelled as isolated reducer peak-memory measurements.

Cold application does not meet the requested FMFT performance range; FG is
closest at about 1.93 times FMFT's measured scalar time. The warm results are
nevertheless promising for workflows that reuse reductions. X has no matched
application-timing result in this set; its numerical correctness experiment
must not be substituted for a scalar-only benchmark.

## 5. What the cache means for integrated UV counterterms

The cache is in-memory **exact memoization**, owned by a RustRed reducer bound
to one family, ordering, rule set and terminal set. Its key is an integral's
integer-power vector. Its value is an exact linear combination of the declared
terminals, with dimension dependence still symbolic. It stores intermediate
reductions too, not just the externally requested answer. It is not a table
of sampled numerical values and does not depend on guessing nearby answers.

For example, reducing a dotted parent traverses many intermediate integrals.
After their decompositions have been stored, asking for that same parent
returns its cached decomposition. A different numerator integral may also
benefit if its descent reaches already cached intermediates, although that
new target can still require significant additional work.

The approximately 34 ms H measurement repeats the **same target** in the same
live reducer. It includes the remaining adapter/master-evaluation work, not
merely a map lookup, and the test verifies that the warm call applies zero new
IBP rules. Recreating the reducer or clearing its cache loses this benefit.
The cache is not currently a persisted on-disk cache carried between processes.

As a rough illustration using these medians, thirteen identical requests would
cost about 38.7 seconds with one cold native reduction and twelve warm calls,
versus about 41.2 seconds at the measured per-call FMFT cost. This arithmetic
is not a measured batch benchmark and assumes FMFT's cost stays unchanged;
it shows why amortized cost, rather than cold latency alone, is relevant here.

It is reasonable to retain family-bound reducers across GammaLoop's integrated
UV-counterterm generation and amortize their cold work across many diagrams
and subgraphs. Repeated scalar keys and overlapping reductions could make this
more representative than a fresh-cache benchmark for every individual input.
But this is a plausible lifecycle strategy, **not yet a measured result for a
real CT-generation campaign**. The experimental four-loop owner has not been
integrated into that complete production lifecycle.

Memory and concurrency also matter. The cache has existing integral/coefficient
storage accounting and limits; a large warmed family is not free. The current
experimental Vakint wrapper protects its mutable reducer with a mutex, so one
shared owner can serialize concurrent reduction calls. Blindly giving every
worker a complete private warmed cache could instead waste substantial RAM.
The next practical measurement should use the actual CT input stream, reporting
unique/repeated targets, new rule work, hit rate, retained memory and cumulative
wall time. That will determine whether warm reuse is sufficient and where cold
optimization or a better sharing policy is still necessary. No such new
infrastructure is being added during this checkpoint.

## 6. Certification, usable interfaces and remaining delivery work

Certification no longer aims to prove that the terminal set is minimal. A
manageable finite nonminimal set is acceptable. The optional proof may also
be restricted to an explicitly requested numerator-rank or power scope.
Nevertheless, a numerator bound alone does not bound positive propagator
powers, and a reduction may leave the starting rank range. A valid scoped
certificate must account for every reachable successor, not just enumerate
starting examples and stop checking when an intermediate exceeds a cutoff.

The existing whole-family verifier separates original-source replay, guard and
domain reasoning, strict descent, finite terminals, coverage, installation and
cold loading. Four-loop attempts have made substantial progress through sector
audits but still encounter later guard/domain or resource obligations. A
successful audit stage is not equivalent to a successfully installed artifact.
Current improvements retain joint affine consequences and try cheaper exact
coefficient proofs before expensive factor work, without topology exceptions.

The checkpoint also exposes two useful, deliberately limited tools. Saved
candidate bundles can be loaded directly into `CandidateReducer` without
regenerating rules. Its `check_targets` method reports finite concrete
reachability and observed power bounds, but **is not a certificate**, even for
those finite targets, because it does not authenticate the formulas' original
IBP provenance. Separately, `SourcePortAudit::replay_sector_rule_batch` checks
selected rule identities and declared guards against original sources. It
does not prove complete reachability, descent or terminal coverage by itself.
Joining these services into a persisted and enforced bounded certificate
remains unfinished.

The current `--max-negative-index-degree` interface is deliberately fail-closed:
requests through degree 30 are recognized but rejected because the
successor-closed proof domain is not yet persisted and enforced, while values
above 30 are input errors. This rank bound is a capability boundary, not a
published rank-30 certificate or an unbounded-certification fallback.

The established public surfaces remain the Rust library, `campaign` CLI and
Python `import rustred`. Generation and certification can be invoked separately
and saved candidates remain available after a failed certification attempt.
RustRed remains topology-generic; the four parent examples are input files,
not embedded solver cases. The new direct candidate loader is presently a
Rust API for experimental consumers, not a promise of a new production CLI or
Python application mode in this checkpoint.
